First-touch grading (triage seat, session `session_014tGY3fzu4uwCoe7HrfUtWg`): **closed, not planned.** The card is the record; reopening is free and the maintainer may veto this close.

Rationale against the three axes: (①) zero measured pull — no org-authored overlay of a public-form view is known to exist, and the filer asserts no disclosure (anonymous callers read the env-wide partition, exactly as before #9454); (②) the fix requires a genuinely new design seam — deriving an owning org for an anonymous request from host/environment — which is a product question ("which org owns an anonymous request on a multi-org deployment?") that should be decided when someone actually needs the answer, not banked now; (③) nothing here lets an agent author something false — the override is unapplied, not silently misapplied.

Restart condition (why this is a close rather than a hold — there is no machine-checkable trigger to hang a hold on): reopen when a real deployment wants an org overlay served on a public form; at that moment this becomes a `needs-user-decision` card with the four-prong block, and the filer's enumeration (17 clean sites, this one structurally out of reach of #9454's session-derived mechanism) is the evidence base to bring.
